candidates.source_name: e-Prokurimi — Kosovo national e-procurement platform (KRPP/PPRC)
candidates.why_relevant: Single mandatory national platform where every Kosovo contracting authority (ministries, municipalities, publicly owned enterprises, independent agencies) publishes contract notices (njoftim per kontrate), tender dossiers and contract award notices (njoftim per dhenie te kontrates), including banking services, payroll/card services, POS acceptance, treasury and payment software. Award notices name the winning economic operator, contract value and technical scope — hard evidence unavailable from vendor press releases.
candidates.source_subtype: national e-procurement portal / tender and award notice database
candidates.access_status: public web portal; browsing notices generally does not require login, bidding does
candidates.legal_status: official government publication, public by law (Law on Public Procurement)
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Prefer the OCDS API/bulk export (see PPRC OCDS entry) for structured harvesting; supplement with targeted portal search by CPV codes for financial/banking services (CPV 66xxxxxx) and IT payment software (CPV 48xxxxxx) plus keyword filters in sq/sr/en; fetch linked notice documents (DokumentPodaciFrm.aspx?id=...) as PDFs.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language (sq) search on seed query + English confirmation search
queries_used: e-prokurimi Kosove njoftim per dhenie te kontrates sherbime bankare
Kosovo public procurement regulatory commission KRPP contract award notices banking services

candidates.source_name: PPRC/KRPP Open Contracting (OCDS) bulk data & API — OCP Data Registry entry
candidates.why_relevant: The Kosovo Public Procurement Regulatory Commission publishes the full e-Prokurimi contracting cycle as Open Contracting Data Standard (OCDS) via API since 2021; the OCP registry mirrors it for download in JSON/Excel/CSV by year or all-time. This is the machine-readable backbone for systematically extracting every banking/payment-services award: buyer, supplier, lots, values, procedure type, dates.
candidates.source_subtype: structured open data mirror / API registry
candidates.legal_status: open data republication of official government data
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Download annual OCDS JSON packages, filter releases by CPV/classification and by item/lot title regex in sq/sr/en (sherbime bankare, bankarske usluge, banking, POS, terminal, kartela, karticа, pagesa/plaćanje, softuer pagesash); reconcile supplier names to bank/PSP entity list.
candidates.discovered_via_method: snowballed from KRPP/e-Prokurimi search into open-contracting ecosystem
queries_used: Kosovo PPRC OCDS API open contracting data standard e-prokurimi API endpoint

candidates.source_name: KRPP / Public Procurement Regulatory Commission (PPRC) institutional site — rules, forms, annual procurement reports
candidates.why_relevant: The regulator's rules and standard forms define the notice taxonomy (B05 njoftim per kontrate, B08 njoftim per dhenie te kontrates, B58 etc.), thresholds, and the multilingual publication obligation for contracts >=EUR 500,000 (sq/sr/en). Essential for building reliable parsers and for knowing which notice types carry award value and scope. KRPP annual reports aggregate spend by category and authority.
candidates.source_subtype: regulator legal framework / standard forms / annual reports
candidates.suggested_collection_method: One-off download of primary and secondary legislation and standard form templates to drive an extraction schema; annual re-check for form/threshold changes; harvest KRPP annual procurement reports for sector aggregates.
candidates.discovered_via_method: search result follow-through from seed query
queries_used: e-prokurimi Kosove njoftim per dhenie te kontrates sherbime bankare
local_language_terms_used: Rregullat dhe Udhezuesi Operativ per Prokurimin Publik

candidates.source_name: Prokurimi i Hapur — Open & Transparent Procurement Portal (Lëvizja FOL / Demokraci Plus, USAID TEAM)
candidates.why_relevant: Civil-society portal that ingests e-Prokurimi data via the OCDS API and presents contracts, contracting authorities and economic operators in a searchable, analyst-friendly way. candidates.suggested_collection_method: Supplier-name search for known banks/PSPs/POS vendors; periodic crawl of contract listing pages; cross-check totals against OCDS data to detect gaps.

candidates.why_relevant: OSHP adjudicates bidder complaints; its decisions reveal who bid, on what technical specification, at what price, and why an award was annulled or upheld — including for banking, card and payment-system tenders. negative_findings.description: No individual, currently published Kosovo contract award notice specifically for commercial banking services, payroll cards, POS acceptance or a treasury/payment software system could be surfaced through general web search in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches in sq, sr and en returned the platform, the regulator, the legal framework and unrelated award PDFs (life insurance at BQK, a customs B08 form, a Tax Administration sr-language notice) but no banking/payment-specific award document. Such notices are almost certainly present but only retrievable inside the e-Prokurimi search interface or the OCDS dataset, which general search engines do not index.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms that this cell cannot be worked from search engines; the collection design must go through the OCDS API / portal query interface with CPV and keyword filters, not through crawling public search results.

negative_findings.description: The exact OCDS API base URL / bulk-download endpoint on the rks-gov.net platform was not established in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Multiple secondary sources (Open Contracting Partnership, OCP Data Registry, Demokraci Plus Red Flags) independently state that KRPP publishes OCDS via an API on rks-gov.net and that data is downloadable in JSON/Excel/CSV, but no source in this pass exposed the literal endpoint string. Recorded as a hypothesis, not a dead end.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The API is the single highest-value collection route for this cell; the exact endpoint must be resolved (via the OCP Data Registry publication page or by inspecting prokurimihapur.org / redflags.dplus.org network calls) before pipeline design.

negative_findings.description: No authoritative Albanian- or Serbian-language CPV label list for financial and banking services (CPV 66xxxxxx) was located in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: The Kosovo procurement rules confirm CPV is used and that large-value notices must be published in sq/sr/en, but the localised CPV vocabulary that would let a collector match category labels exactly was not retrieved.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Without the localised CPV label set, keyword matching on sq/sr notice titles will be lossy and may miss awards phrased in non-obvious ways (e.g. 'sherbime financiare', 'mirembajtje e sistemit te pagesave').

negative_findings.description: Commercial aggregators covering Kosovo tenders (DevelopmentAid, BidsFactory) are subscription- or registration-gated.
negative_findings.result_summary: Listing pages are visible in search results but full tender and award text is behind a paywall; treated as blocked rather than absent.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: These cannot serve as a primary feed; the design must rely on the official portal and OCDS data, using aggregators only for alerting or translation.

negative_findings.description: Whether Kosovo municipalities and POEs procure banking services competitively at all, or hold them under legacy/non-tendered arrangements, could not be determined.
negative_findings.result_summary: No evidence either way surfaced in this pass. National Audit Office reports were identified as the place where such non-competitive or legacy banking arrangements would be criticised, but the specific finding was not located.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: If most public-sector banking relationships are untendered legacy arrangements, procurement notices will systematically under-represent the real market and audit reports become the primary evidence channel instead.

coverage_gaps.description: The e-Prokurimi search interface and the OCDS API have not been exercised; no query pattern, pagination behaviour, rate limits or bot defences are known.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated technical probe: resolve the OCDS endpoint from the OCP Data Registry publication page, pull one annual package, and separately test the portal's notice search with CPV 66xxxxxx and 48xxxxxx filters. Record whether the portal search requires a session/login.

coverage_gaps.description: No enumerated list of Kosovo contracting authorities (ministries, ~38 municipalities, central and ~55 local POEs, independent agencies) was assembled, so buyer-side filtering cannot yet be exhaustive.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Scrape the NJPMNP central/local POE lists and the KRPP contracting-authority register into an entity table with sq/sr/en name variants and common acronyms (KEK, KOSTT, Posta e Kosoves, KRU, ATK/PAK, Dogana).

coverage_gaps.description: Serbian-language coverage of Kosovo-government procurement notices is thin — only one sr-language award notice (Tax Administration) and the sr version of BQK procurement rules were found, plus Serbia's own parallel channel.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Systematically test whether e-Prokurimi exposes sr-language notice text for large-value contracts, and build an sr keyword set (bankarske usluge, platni promet, platne kartice, POS terminali, trezor) for portal/OCDS querying.

coverage_gaps.description: Structured coverage appears to start around 2020-2021 (OCDS API, Red Flags); pre-2020 municipal and central awards are only partly represented by the Open Data Kosovo dataset.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Assess whether OCDS all-time export truly reaches back before 2020; if not, evaluate the ODK municipal dataset and National Audit Office reports as the historical layer.

coverage_gaps.description: Award notices give winner and value but usually not full technical specification; the tender dossier and signed contract carry the scope (number of POS terminals, card volumes, SLA) that matters commercially.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Test whether e-Prokurimi and AQP expose tender dossiers and signed contract PDFs for financial-services procurements, and whether OSHP decision files can substitute where the dossier is not published.

coverage_gaps.description: Donor- and IFI-funded procurement (World Bank, UNDP, EU/IPA, EBRD, KfW, GIZ) affecting Kosovo payment infrastructure runs entirely outside e-Prokurimi and was only sampled here; EU/IPA and EBRD channels were not searched.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add dedicated probes of EU TED / IPA procurement for Kosovo, EBRD procurement notices, and KfW/GIZ tender pages, in en and where available sq.

brief: Kosovo's public-sector buying route is unusually well-centralised for the region: e-Prokurimi (KRPP/PPRC) is the mandatory publication point for contract and award notices across ministries, ~38 municipalities and central/local publicly owned enterprises, and since 2021 it is exposed as an Open Contracting Data Standard API with bulk JSON/Excel/CSV downloads mirrored in the OCP Data Registry — making systematic, structured harvesting of banking, card, POS and payment-software awards genuinely feasible. Around that core sit high-value secondary layers: OSHP review-body decisions (which expose bidder pricing and technical disqualification detail absent from award notices), the National Audit Office's annual reports on budget organisations and POEs, the Central Bank of Kosovo's own tender page (the key window on national payment-infrastructure procurement), the Central Procurement Agency's framework contracts, and mature civil-society mirrors (prokurimihapur.org, Red Flags/Demokraci Plus, Open Data Kosovo) that are often more queryable than the official portal. The main caveats are that general web search does not index individual notices — this cell must be worked through the API/portal query interface, not crawling — that Serbian-language notice coverage is confirmed to exist but is thin in practice, and that a parallel Serbia-funded spending channel for northern municipalities sits entirely outside the Kosovo system. Priority next steps are resolving the literal OCDS endpoint, building an sq/sr/en keyword and localised-CPV set, and enumerating contracting authorities and POEs as buyer-side filters.
